texts: mixed: the rule itself is right and usable - first-year apprentices as the doers, "usually" carried as the strength of the habit, and the cisterns as one definite group - but the parse also asserts something your sentence never says, that a first-year apprentice is a kind of "first year", which came from unpacking the hyphenated label as if it named a category. No content is lost, so no rewrite is needed on content grounds: this is the translator over-unpacking a compound label, not a fault in your wording, and rephrasing the tenure as a phrase ("apprentices in their first year") risks the worse outcome of the restriction being dropped or landing in a rule condition that can never match. If you would rather avoid hyphenated kind-labels of this shape altogether, "New apprentices usually fill the cisterns." parses without the stray claim - but adopt it only if "new" is faithful to your lore, since it loosens the exact first-year tenure.
